facts.statement: The genus Torosaurus was named by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1891.
facts.quote: authority: Marsh, 1891

facts.statement: Fossils of Torosaurus have been found across the Western Interior of North America, ranging from Saskatchewan to Texas.
facts.quote: Fossils which have been definitively identified as Torosaurus or which might belong to it have been discovered across the Western Interior of North America, from as far north as Saskatchewan to as far south as Texas

facts.statement: Torosaurus measured between 7.5 and 9 meters in length and weighed approximately 8 metric tons.
facts.quote: Measuring between 7.5 and 9 m and weighing around 8 MT

facts.statement: In 1891, John Bell Hatcher discovered a pair of ceratopsian skulls with elongated, perforated frills in Niobrara County, southeastern Wyoming.
facts.quote: In 1891, two years after the naming of Triceratops, a pair of ceratopsian skulls with elongated frills bearing holes were found by John Bell Hatcher in Niobrara County in southeastern Wyoming

facts.statement: The name Torosaurus is likely derived from the Greek verb 'toreo,' meaning 'to perforate,' rather than being a mistranslation of 'bull lizard'.
facts.quote: The name Torosaurus is frequently mistranslated as "bull lizard" from the Latin noun taurus or the Spanish word toro, but is much more likely derived from the Greek verb (toreo), which means "to perforate"

facts.statement: In 1896, Marsh explained that the open perforations in the parietal bones suggested the name Torosaurus and separated it from other known ceratopsids.
facts.quote: In 1896, Marsh explained: "The open perforations in the parietal, which have suggested the name Torosaurus, readily separate this genus from all the gigantic species hitherto known in the Ceratopsidae..."

facts.statement: The type species T. latus is based on holotype YPM 1830, which is a partial skull.
facts.quote: T. latus was based on holotype YPM 1830, which is a partial skull

facts.statement: The holotype for the species T. gladius was specimen YPM 1831, which is an even larger skull than the type species.
facts.quote: The holotype of T. gladius was specimen YPM 1831, which is an even larger skull

facts.statement: The holotypes for both T. latus and T. gladius were found in the Lance Formation of the late Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: Both fossils were found in the Lance Formation of the late Maastrichtian

facts.statement: In 1976, Douglas Lawson renamed the species Arrhinoceratops? utahensis to Torosaurus utahensis.
facts.quote: In 1976, it was renamed to Torosaurus utahensis by Douglas Lawson

facts.statement: In 2010, a study suggested that Torosaurus might represent the mature growth stage of Triceratops, characterized by an elongated frill and holes appearing during maturation.
facts.quote: In 2010, the validity of Torosaurus was disputed. A study of fossil bone histology combined with an investigation of frill shape concluded that Torosaurus probably represented the mature form of Triceratops

facts.statement: Studies from 2011 to 2013 argued that morphological differences between Torosaurus and Triceratops prevent them from being the same genus.
facts.quote: In 2011, 2012, and 2013, however, studies of external features of known specimens have claimed that morphological differences between the two genera preclude their synonymy

facts.statement: It is currently debated whether T. utahensis should be considered a distinct genus or the mature growth stage of a Triceratops species, similar to the hypothesis for T. latus.
facts.quote: Research has not yet been published on whether T. utahensis should be regarded as a new genus or, as has been suggested for T. latus, the mature growth stage of a species of Triceratops

facts.statement: Torosaurus individuals were large, measuring between 7.5 and 9 meters in length and weighing between 6 and 11 metric tons.
facts.quote: The individuals referred to Torosaurus are all large, comparable to the largest Triceratops specimens, measuring 7.5 to 9 m long and weighing 6 - 11 MT.

facts.statement: Torosaurus possessed an especially long skull due to its elongated frill.
facts.quote: Due to the elongated frill, the skull length is especially considerable.

facts.statement: Hatcher estimated the skull of specimen YPM 1830 to be 2.2 meters long and YPM 1831 to be 2.35 meters long.
facts.quote: Hatcher estimated the skull of YPM 1830 at 2.2 m and that of YPM 1831 at 2.35 m.

facts.statement: The rear edge of the Torosaurus frill bears ten or more epiparietals, which are triangular osteoderms.
facts.quote: The rear edge of the frill bears ten or more epiperietals, or triangular osteoderms.

facts.statement: The Torosaurus parietal bone is thin and contains circular or transversely oval openings called parietal fenestrae.
facts.quote: The parietal bone is thin and pierced by parietal fenestrae in the form of circular or transversely ovular openings.

facts.statement: The Torosaurus parietal bone is approximately 20% wider than it is long.
facts.quote: The parietal bone is about 20% wider than it is long.

facts.statement: The Torosaurus squamosal bone features a conspicuous ridge along its edge with the parietal, accompanied by a deep longitudinal trough parallel to it.
facts.quote: Its squamosal bore a conspicuous ridge on the edge with the parietal combined with a deep longitudinal trough parallel to it.

facts.statement: The orbital horns of Torosaurus vary, being large and curved forward in MOR 981, or short and straight in MOR 1122 and ANSP 15191.
facts.quote: The orbital "brow" horns are sometimes large and curved to the front, as with MOR 981, or sometimes short and straight, as shown by MOR 1122 and ANSP 15191.

facts.statement: In specimen YPM 1831, the orbital horns originate at the rear edge of the eye socket.
facts.quote: With YPM 1831, however, they originate at the rear edge of the orbit.

facts.statement: The frill of specimen YPM 1831 is heart-shaped with a midline notch, while the rear edges of other specimens are straight.
facts.quote: The frill of YPM 1831 is also heart-shaped, with a clear midline notch, whereas the rear edge of the other specimens is straight.

facts.statement: The frill of YPM 1831 has a length-width ratio of 1.26, while the frill of MOR 981 is 2.28 times longer than it is wide.
facts.quote: With YPM 1831, the length-width ratio is 1.26, but MOR 981 has a shield 2.28 times longer than it is wide.

facts.statement: Specimen MOR 981 has ten epiparietals and MOR 1122 has twelve.
facts.quote: MOR 981 and MOR 1122 have ten and twelve epiparietals, respectively.

facts.statement: The well-preserved skull of the Torosaurus specimen nicknamed "Adam", displayed in 2023, is the largest known at 3 meters long.
facts.quote: The well preserved skull of the Torosaurus specimen nicknamed "Adam", first put on display in 2023, is the largest known at 3 m long.

facts.statement: Torosaurus has traditionally been classified in the subfamily Chasmosaurinae due to its long frill.
facts.quote: Torosaurus has, with its long frill, traditionally been classified in Chasmosaurinae.

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis in the 1990s showed that both Torosaurus and Triceratops belong to the subfamily Chasmosaurinae.
facts.quote: However, in the 1990s, exact cladistic analysis showed that both genera were chasmosaurines.

facts.statement: In 1998, Thomas Lehman claimed that a Pentaceratops specimen had a skull that would have been 2.9 meters long in life.
facts.quote: In 1998, however, Thomas Lehman claimed that a Pentaceratops specimen possessed a partial skull that would have been 2.9 m long in life.

facts.statement: In 2006, Andrew Farke noted that new skulls he described were longer on average than Hatcher's original specimens.
facts.quote: Furthermore, in 2006, Andrew Farke had pointed out that the new skulls described by him were even longer on average than Hatcher's original two.

facts.statement: Andrew Farke argued that no systematic differences exist between Torosaurus and Triceratops apart from the frill.
facts.quote: Farke stressed that, apart from the frill, no systematic differences could be found between Torosaurus and Triceratops.

facts.statement: In 2008, Hunt concluded that T. utahensis possessed a midline epiparietal, unlike T. latus but similar to Triceratops.
facts.quote: In 2008, Hunt concluded that T. utahensis, contrary to T. latus, but similar to Triceratops, possessed a midline epiparietal.

facts.statement: Torosaurus lived during the Maastrichtian age in the Laramidia region.
facts.quote: In the Maastrichtian age of Laramidia, two closely related chasmosaurines shared the same habitat.

facts.statement: The primary difference between Torosaurus and Triceratops was the shape of their frills.
facts.quote: The only discernible difference between them was the form of the frill.

facts.statement: In 2009, John Scannella proposed that Torosaurus and Triceratops were growth stages of the same genus based on his study of fossils in the Hell Creek Formation.
facts.quote: In 2009, John Scannella, investigating dinosaur ontogeny in the Hell Creek Formation of Montana, concluded that this situation could be best explained by the hypothesis that Triceratops and Torosaurus were growth stages of a single genus.

facts.statement: Jack Horner argued that the frills of ceratopsians were made of metaplastic bone, which can change shape over time.
facts.quote: Horner stressed that the frill of ceratopsian skulls consisted of metaplastic bone.

facts.statement: A problem with the hypothesis is that Torosaurus fossils are rare, despite being expected to be common if it were the final maturation phase of Triceratops.
facts.quote: One problem was that if Torosaurus were the normal last maturation phase of Triceratops, which they called the "toromorph phase", it would be expected that Torosaurus fossils were quite common, whereas in fact they are fairly rare.

facts.statement: Andrew Farke noted that the holes in Nedoceratops frills were surrounded by thick bone swellings rather than thinning bone.
facts.quote: Farke pointed out that the irregular holes in the Nedoceratops frill, far from piercing thinning bone, were surrounded by thick swellings.

facts.statement: Andrew Farke stated that the number of epoccipitals generally does not increase as ceratopsian frills grow.
facts.quote: In general, the number of epoccipitals in ceratopsians does not increase when the frill grows.

facts.statement: Farke argued that the formation of holes in ceratopsian frills is not age-related, as young individuals often possess them.
facts.quote: Likewise, with Ceratopia in general, the formation of holes in the frill is not related to age, as even the youngest individuals often possess the parietal fenestrae.

facts.statement: Many Triceratops specimens exhibit deeply veined frill surfaces that indicate considerable age.
facts.quote: Many Triceratops specimens have frills with a deeply veined surface, indicating considerable age.

facts.statement: The conclusions of Scannella and Horner regarding the relationship between Torosaurus and Triceratops have not been widely accepted by the scientific community.
facts.quote: Scannella and Horner's conclusions have not been widely accepted.

facts.statement: Researchers consider the idea that Torosaurus frill holes formed after the bone was rejuvenated and granulated again to be an unlikely sequence.
facts.quote: The bone of their frills would have to be rejuvenated and then become granulated again in order for hole formation to begin, which Farke considered to be an unlikely sequence.

facts.statement: Specimen YPM 1831 is considered a subadult Torosaurus because its unfused sutures and smooth bone texture indicate it was not fully grown despite its large size.
facts.quote: Finally, Farke pointed out that specimen YPM 1831, despite its enormous size, was apparently not yet fully-grown, as shown by its unfused sutures and smooth bone texture.

facts.statement: Scanella and Horner argued that Nedoceratops was likely a diseased individual of Triceratops rather than a distinct genus.
facts.quote: Taking all the evidence into consideration, they thought it much more likely that Nedoceratops represented a diseased individual of Triceratops than a genus of its own.

facts.statement: Some researchers suggest that Torosaurus latus specimens found in older layers might represent an early stage of Triceratops evolution through anagenesis.
facts.quote: Alternatively, the Torosaurus latus specimens, having been found in older layers, might, in a process of anagenesis, represent an early stage of Triceratops evolution.

facts.statement: The number of epiparietals appears to have gradually decreased over time, with the oldest dated specimen MOR 1122 having twelve and the younger MOR 981 having ten.
facts.quote: The oldest specimen that can be dated, MOR 1122, has twelve epiparietals, while the younger MOR 981 possesses ten, seeming to indicate an evolutionary sequence in which the number of epiparietals gradually decreased.

facts.statement: Longrich proposed testing the hypothesis that Torosaurus and Triceratops are the same species by deriving three specific predictions from it.
facts.quote: Longrich argued that the "toromorph" hypothesis implied three such predictions.

facts.statement: The geographical ranges of Torosaurus and Triceratops do not perfectly coincide, with no Torosaurus fossils found in the far north and only Torosaurus utahensis known from the south.
facts.quote: In fact, their geographical ranges do not perfectly coincide. In the very north, no Torosaurus fossils have been found, while from the south, only Torosaurus utahensis is known.

facts.statement: Analysis of skull element fusion sequences revealed that most Torosaurus specimens were very old, though two exceptions were found.
facts.quote: It transpired that the fusion typically took place in a certain sequence, providing additional information about their age.

facts.statement: Specimen ANSP 15192 was identified as a relatively young adult Torosaurus due to the lack of fusion in its snout bones.
facts.quote: The small individual ANSP 15192 was a relatively young adult, as shown by the lack of fusion of the snout bones.

facts.statement: Specimen YPM 1831 was the youngest Torosaurus specimen studied, characterized by an unfused snout, epijugal, and occipital condyle.
facts.quote: The youngest specimen was YPM 1831, with an unfused snout, epijugal, and occipital condyle.

facts.statement: Longrich concluded that the hypothesis was refuted because the prediction that all Torosaurus specimens were adults was not supported by the evidence.
facts.quote: Longrich concluded that the test of the second prediction refuted the hypothesis.

facts.statement: Longrich considered the thin areas on Triceratops frills as potential precursors to parietal fenestrae, viewing them as the strongest evidence for a transitional phase.
facts.quote: Longrich considered the claim that the thin areas on Triceratops frills were precursors of parietal fenestrae, as the strongest proof of a transitional phase.

facts.statement: Longrich noted that the thin areas on Triceratops frills differ from Torosaurus holes in position, as the former are partly on the squamosal while the latter are fully surrounded by the parietal.
facts.quote: However, he pointed out that these structures differed in position. The Triceratops depressions are partly located on the squamosal, while the Torosaurus holes are fully surrounded by the parietal.

facts.statement: The depressions on Triceratops frills are bordered by much thicker bone compared to the thin bone surrounding the holes in Torosaurus.
facts.quote: Furthermore, the depressions are bordered by much thicker bone, while the Torosaurus holes are surrounded by thin bone.

facts.statement: Longrich concluded that the hypothesis that Torosaurus and Triceratops are the same species should be rejected because it was refuted in two of the three tested predictions.
facts.quote: Being refuted in two of the three predictions, the hypothesis should be rejected.

facts.statement: Torosaurus lived during the Late Maastrichtian stage of the Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: The same study also noted that Torosaurus indeed lived during the Late Maastrichtian.

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Torosaurus is Torosaurus latus.
facts.quote: type_species: Torosaurus latus

facts.statement: Torosaurus utahensis is a recognized species within the genus, described by Lawson in 1976.
facts.quote: subdivision: Torosaurus utahensis Lawson, 1976

facts.statement: Torosaurus lived in North America during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 72 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivieron a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 72 a 66 millones de años, en el Maastrichtiense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: The temporal range of Torosaurus may extend back to 69 million years ago.
facts.quote: El rango temporal podría extenderse hasta hace 69 millones de años.

facts.statement: Fossils of Torosaurus have been found in western North America, ranging from Saskatchewan to southern Texas.
facts.quote: Se han descubierto fósiles en el interior occidental de América del Norte, desde Saskatchewan hasta el sur de Texas.

facts.statement: Torosaurus possessed one of the largest skulls found in any terrestrial animal.
facts.quote: Poseían uno de los más grandes cráneos encontrados en un animal terrestre.

facts.statement: The skull with the frill of Torosaurus measured approximately 2.8 meters in length.
facts.quote: El cráneo con la gola medía alrededor de 2,8 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Torosaurus was approximately 8.8 meters long, 2 meters tall, and weighed between 4 and 6 tons.
facts.quote: De la cabeza a la cola, Torosaurus debe haber rondado los 8,8 metros de largo, 2 metros de alto y haber pesado entre 4 y 6 toneladas.

facts.statement: Torosaurus is distinguished by an elongated frill with large openings called fenestrae, long squamosal bones with a channel on top, and five or more pairs of epiparietal horns on the back of the frill.
facts.quote: Se distingue por un volante alargado con grandes aberturas, llamadas fenestras, huesos escamosos largos del volante con un canal en su superficie superior y la presencia de cinco o más pares de cuernos, epoccipitales, en la parte posterior del volante.

facts.statement: Torosaurus had a short horn over its beak and two longer horns over its eyes, which provided protection against predators.
facts.quote: Un cuerno corto sobre su pico de loro y dos cuernos más largos sobre sus ojos que le proporciona la protección contra depredadores.

facts.statement: The horns of Torosaurus were possibly used in rivalry during courtship.
facts.quote: Los cuernos también fueron utilizados posiblemente en rivalidad durante el cortejo.

facts.statement: Torosaurus had the second-largest skull of any land animal, surpassed only by Pentaceratops.
facts.quote: Torosaurus fue el animal con el segundo cranéo más grande que caminó por la tierra, el que tenía el cráneo más grande fue el Pentaceratops.

facts.statement: Unlike Triceratops prorsus, Torosaurus lacked a long nasal horn and instead resembled the earlier Triceratops horridus with a short nasal horn.
facts.quote: Torosaurus también carecía del cuerno de nariz largo que se ve en Triceratops prorsus y en cambio se parecía al anterior y más basal Triceratops horridus por tener un cuerno de nariz corto.

facts.statement: Three species of Torosaurus have been named, but T. gladius is no longer considered a valid species.
facts.quote: Se han nombrado tres especies, Torosaurus latus , Torosaurus gladius y Torosaurus utahensis. Sin embargo, T. gladius ya no se considera una especie válida.

facts.statement: Longrich suggested that specific Torosaurus specimens were outliers in growth sequences, indicating their elongated squamosals could not be explained by allometry alone.
facts.quote: Longrich pointed out that when Torosaurus and Triceratops specimens are combined to create a single growth sequence, as Scanella and Horner had done, Torosaurus specimens ANSP 15192 and YPM 1831 were outliers relative to the regression line because their squamosals were more elongated than could be explained by allometry.

facts.statement: Longrich anticipated that proponents of the Torosaurus-Triceratops synonymy would attribute morphological differences to individual variation.
facts.quote: Longrich foresaw that Scanella and Horner would respond to his second test of their hypothesis by claiming that its results were caused by individual variation.

facts.statement: A 2013 morphometric study by Farke was inconclusive regarding the status of Torosaurus utahensis, as its morphospace fell between Triceratops and Torosaurus latus without clear separation.
facts.quote: Farke's 2013 morphometric study was inconclusive on this point, with T. utahensis morphospace falling in between Triceratops and Torosaurus latus and not well separated from either.

facts.statement: Studies from 2011 to 2013 argued that external morphological differences between Torosaurus and Triceratops prevent them from being synonyms.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en 2011, 2012 y 2013, los estudios de características externas de especímenes conocidos han afirmado que las diferencias morfológicas entre los dos géneros impiden su sinonimia.

facts.statement: The hypothesis that epiparietal horns were formed by splitting osteoderms via erosion has only been established for episquamosals, not epiparietals.
facts.quote: The proposed splitting of osteoderms by erosion has only been established with episquamosals, never with epiparietals.

facts.statement: Torosaurus was similar in size to contemporary Triceratops but distinguished by an elongated frill with large fenestrae, long squamosal bones with a dorsal channel, and five or more pairs of epiparietal horns.
facts.quote: Torosaurus tenía el mismo tamaño que el contemporáneo Triceratops, pero se distingue por un volante alargado con grandes aberturas, llamadas fenestras, huesos escamosos largos del volante con un canal en su superficie superior y la presencia de cinco o más pares de cuernos, epoccipitales, en la parte posterior del volante.

facts.statement: Torosaurus individuals are all large, comparable to the largest Triceratops specimens.
facts.quote: Los individuos a los que se hace referencia como Torosaurus son todos grandes, comparables a los especímenes más grandes de Triceratops.

facts.statement: Hatcher estimated the skull of YPM 1830 to be 2.2 meters long and YPM 1831 to be 2.35 meters long.
facts.quote: Hatcher estimó el cráneo de YPM 1830 en 2,2 metros y el de YPM 1831 en 2,35 metros.

facts.statement: In 2006, Andrew Farke established some diagnostic traits for Torosaurus.
facts.quote: Farke en 2006 estableció algunos rasgos de diagnóstico de Torosaurus.

facts.statement: The frill is extremely long compared to the rest of the skull.
facts.quote: El volante es extremadamente largo en comparación con el resto del cráneo.

facts.statement: The posterior parietal edge of the frill has ten or more triangular osteoderms called epiparietals.
facts.quote: El borde posterior, parietal, del volante tiene diez o más epiparietales, osteodermos triangulares.

facts.statement: The parietal bone is thin and perforated by parietal fenestrae in the shape of circular or transversely oval openings.
facts.quote: El hueso parietal es delgado. Está perforado por fenestras parietales en forma de aberturas circulares o transversalmente ovaladas.

facts.statement: The parietal bone is approximately 20% wider than it is long.
facts.quote: El hueso parietal es aproximadamente un 20% más ancho que largo.

facts.statement: Farke identified a unique trait distinguishing T. latus from Triceratops horridus and T. utahensis: its squamosal had a conspicuous crest at the border with the parietal combined with a deep longitudinal canal parallel to it.
facts.quote: Farke identificó un único rasgo en el que T. latus difería tanto de Triceratops horridus como de T. utahensis, su esquamosal tenía una cresta conspicua en el borde con el parietal combinado con un profundo canal longitudinal paralelo a él.

facts.statement: The orbital brow horns are sometimes large and curved forward, as in MOR 981, or sometimes short and straight, as shown in MOR 1122 and ANSP 15191.
facts.quote: Los cuernos de "ceja" orbitales son a veces grandes y curvados hacia el frente, como con MOR 981, a veces cortos y rectos como se muestra en MOR 1122 y ANSP 15191.

facts.statement: YPM 1831 and, to a lesser extent, YPM 1830 have a straight, erect nasal horn, whereas MOR 981, ANSP 15192, and especially MOR 1122 have at most a low bump.
facts.quote: YPM 1831 y, en menor medida, YPM 1830 tienen un cuerno nasal recto y erguido, pero MOR 981, ANSP 15192 y especialmente MOR 1122, como mucho, poseen una protuberancia baja.

facts.statement: The frill of YPM 1831 is heart-shaped with a clear notch in the midline, while the posterior edge of other specimens is straight.
facts.quote: El volante de YPM 1831 también tiene forma de corazón, con una muesca clara en la línea media, mientras que el borde posterior de los otros especímenes es recto.

facts.statement: MOR 981 and MOR 1122 have ten and twelve epiparietals respectively.
facts.quote: MOR 981 y MOR 1122 tienen diez y doce epiparietales respectivamente.

facts.statement: Farke emphasized that, apart from the frill, no systematic differences could be found between Torosaurus and Triceratops.
facts.quote: Farke enfatizó que, aparte del volante, no se pudieron encontrar diferencias sistemáticas entre Torosaurus y Triceratops.

facts.statement: In 1891, two ceratopsian skulls with long frills perforated by large holes were found in southeastern Wyoming by John Bell Hatcher.
facts.quote: En 1891, dos años después del descubrimiento de Triceratops, un par de cráneos de ceratopsiano con las golas alargadas perforadas de grandes agujeros fueron encontrados en el sudeste de Wyoming , en el condado de Niobrara, por de John Bell Hatcher.

facts.statement: The paleontologist Othniel Charles Marsh named the genus Torosaurus for these skulls.
facts.quote: Su empleador, el paleontólogo Othniel Charles Marsh acuñó el género Torosaurus para ellos.

facts.statement: The type species T. latus was described by Marsh in 1891, while T. utahensis was described by Lawson in 1976.
facts.quote: T. latus por Marsh en 1891, que es la especie tipo, y T. utahensis, descrita por Lawson en 1976.

facts.statement: The holotype for T. gladius was specimen YPM 1831, a larger skull.
facts.quote: El holotipo de T. gladius fue el espécimen YPM 1831, un cráneo más grande.

facts.statement: Both fossils were found in the Lance Formation, which dates to the Maastrichtian stage.
facts.quote: Ambos fósiles se encontraron en la Formación Lance, que data del Maastrichtiense.

facts.statement: Similar specimens have been found since then in Wyoming, Montana, South Dakota, North Dakota, Utah, and Saskatchewan.
facts.quote: Los especímenes similares se han encontrado desde entonces en Wyoming, Montana, Dakota del Sur, Dakota del Norte, Utah y Saskatchewan.

facts.statement: Paleontologists have observed that Torosaurus specimens are relatively rare in the fossil record compared to the more abundant Triceratops.
facts.quote: Los paleontólogos han observado que los especímenes de Torosaurus son relativamente infrecuentes en el expediente fósil, mientras que Triceratops es más abundante.

facts.statement: Juvenile individuals were excavated from the Javelina Formation in Big Bend National Park and identified as Torosaurus cf. utahensis based on their proximity to adults with characteristic Torosaurus skulls.
facts.quote: Se han excavado a los individuos juveniles de la Formación Javelina del parque nacional de Big Bend, identificados como Torosaurus cf. utahensis de acuerdo con su proximidad a los adultos con cráneos característicos de Torosaurus.

facts.statement: Torosaurus belongs to the parent group Triceratopsini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Triceratopsini

facts.statement: Torosaurus is classified in the family Ceratopsidae.
facts.quote: Family: Ceratopsidae

facts.statement: Torosaurus is a member of the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Torosaurus lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: A debate has arisen regarding the possibility that Torosaurus is identical to Triceratops.
facts.quote: Ha surgido un debate sobre la posibilidad de que Torosaurus sea idéntico a Triceratops.

facts.statement: In 2009, John Scannella concluded that Triceratops and Torosaurus could be growth stages of a single genus based on his study of dinosaur ontogeny in the Hell Creek Formation.
facts.quote: En 2009 John Scannella, investigando la ontogenia de los dinosaurios en la Formación Hell Creek de Montana, concluyó que esta situación podría explicarse mejor por la hipótesis de que Triceratops y Torosaurus eran etapas de crecimiento de un solo género.

facts.statement: In 2010, Scanella and Jack Horner concluded that Torosaurus represents the mature form of Triceratops after studying growth patterns in thirty-eight skulls from the Hell Creek Formation.
facts.quote: En 2010, Scanella y Jack Horner, el mentor de Scannella en la Universidad Estatal de Montana, publicaron una investigación sobre los patrones de crecimiento en treinta y ocho especímenes de cráneo, veintinueve de Triceratops , nueve de Torosaurus, de la formación Hell Creek. Llegaron a la conclusión de que Torosaurus de hecho representa la forma madura de Triceratops.

facts.statement: Horner emphasized that ceratopsian frills consisted of metaplastic bone, which can lengthen and shorten over time by extending and reabsorbing to form new shapes.
facts.quote: Horner enfatizó que el volante de los cráneos ceratopsianos consistía en hueso metaplásico. Una característica del hueso metaplásico es que puede alargarse y acortarse con el tiempo, extendiéndose y reabsorbiéndose para formar nuevas formas.

facts.statement: Despite common belief, Torosaurus does not mean 'bull lizard' but rather 'perforated lizard', derived from the ancient Greek word for perforated.
facts.quote: Aunque se piense lo contrario Torosaurus no significa “lagarto toro”, del latín taurus, toro, sino que significa “lagarto perforado” de la palabra del griego antiguo toreo, perforado.

rejected.statement: Torosaurus lived during the Maastrichtian stage of the Cretaceous Period, between 68 and 66 million years ago.
rejected.quote: lived during the Maastrichtian Stage of the Cretaceous Period between 68 and 66 million years ago
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'Period between 68 and 66 million years ago'

rejected.statement: Torosaurus possessed the longest skull of any known land animal, with the frilled skull reaching 2.77 meters in length.
